instruction: I want to help children distinguish word lengths by color. Can you color short words (1-3 letters) in green and longer words (4+ letters) in yellow?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires coloring words by length: green for 1-3 letters, yellow for 4+ letters. Verified from word list: 27 short words (all, do, no, say, am, etc.) should be green, 25 long words (want, four, good, that, etc.) should be yellow. Uses fuzzy color matching with threshold=20.0 since instruction mentions color names.

llm_judge_reasons: CRITICAL: Metric only checks words inside document.tables (line 44), missing all words in regular paragraphs outside tables

CRITICAL: Word length logic is flawed - treats entire run.text as a single word instead of splitting into individual words. If run.text='I am' (4 chars with space), it checks for yellow color instead of treating 'I' and 'am' as separate short words requiring green
CRITICAL: Uncolored words are silently skipped (line 50 condition). If words exist but have no color, evaluator should fail since task requires coloring ALL words
MAJOR: Color comparison may fail - compares RGBColor objects directly without proper attribute access (run.font.color.rgb is already an RGBColor, not a tuple)
Coverage incomplete: Most LibreOffice Writer documents have text in document.paragraphs, not in tables. The metric will return 1.0 (pass) even if no words are checked
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Iterate through document.paragraphs (top-level) in addition to or instead of document.tables
Split run.text into individual words using .split() before checking each word's length
Fail (return 0.0) when words exist but have no color applied
Fix color comparison: extract RGB components as tuple (run.font.color.rgb.r, run.font.color.rgb.g, run.font.color.rgb.b) or convert to tuple before comparison
Add logging to track how many words were checked vs expected to ensure coverage
